# everything they say, in data/characters/bosses/ and data/characters/rivals/ (same scenes, same
# rules, just no NAME: in front). This file is for everybody else: random drivers and the cops.
#
# HOW A LINE LOOKS
#     NAME: what they say
#     NAME (chasing): only said when they start behind you
#     NAME (leading): only said when they start in front of you
#
#   - " / " splits a line into boxes. Each box stays up for a moment by how many words it has, then
#     the next one comes up by itself. Keep boxes short (a dozen words or so).
#   - (chasing) / (leading) are about where the talker starts: in battle mode that's who chases, in a
#     normal race it's the grid. Leave it off and the line works either way. So anything about "your
#     mirrors" or "your bumper" is (chasing), anything about "my tail lights" is (leading).
#   - Fill-ins: {you} = the player's name, {yourcar} = the player's car, {name} = the talker's name,
#     {car} = the talker's car, {yourmake} / {yourmodel} / {youryear} = the player's car's make
#     ("Volks"), model ("GTI Mk5 2.0T") and year.
#   - Add as many lines as you like under a scene. Everybody works through their lines in turn, so
#     nobody repeats themselves until they've said them all.
#
# SCENES (put "SCENE: <one of these>" above the lines; "you" = the player, "they" = whoever's talking)
#   before the race        the call before the countdown
#   the run back           battle mode turned round at the end of the road
#   you crash              you hit something hard
#   they crash             they hit something hard
#   you hit them           you ran into them
#   they're on your bumper they're right behind you
#   you're on their bumper you're right behind them
#   you fall way back      you're way behind them
#   they fall way back     they're way behind you
#   they pass you          they got past you
#   you pass them          you got past them
#   their bar is low       battle: their health bar is nearly empty
#   your bar is low        battle: your health bar is nearly empty
#   they win / they lose   battle over
#   mid race               nothing happened, they just talk (every minute or so)
#   your car               something about the player's car (also mid race)
#   your car: <tag>        ... only when the player's car is one: an id (gti_mk5...), a family (civic,
#                          miata, rx7, mr2, impreza, golf, mopar), a body (sedan, coupe, hatch, wagon,
#                          sports, muscle, pickup, suv, van), fwd/rwd/awd, turbo/na, rotary, v8, old/90s/
#                          00s/new, heavy/tiny, wing, lowered, lifted, loud, fun, tired
#                          (data/characters/README.txt has the full list)
#   cops only: a cop spots you, the chase starts, heat 2, heat 3, heat 4, heat 5, you PIT a cop,
#              you lose the cops
#
# WHO'S WHO (the NAME before the colon; capitals or not, it doesn't matter)
#   ANYONE: any random driver. A boss or rival with no line of their own for a mid-race scene says
#           ANYONE's (a rival tries their style's line first).
#   A boss or rival by name (PEYLIX, MUTTT, DALE...) works here too, on top of their own file.
#   Random drivers before the race get a few lines picked for them (once, then they keep them) from
#   ANYONE plus their style and quirk:
#     styles: SMOOTH DRIVER, AGGRESSIVE DRIVER, SIDEWAYS DRIVER, LATE BRAKER, STEADY DRIVER, WILD DRIVER
#     quirks: FLASHER, SNEAKY PASSER, RAMMER, DRIFTER, HONKER, JUMPER, CAREFUL DRIVER,
#             HANDBRAKE ADDICT, TAILGATER
#     (mid-race a random driver says their style's line for that scene if there is one, else ANYONE's)
#   COPS: the police radio.
#
# TYPOS ARE SAFE: a line with a name or scene the game doesn't know is skipped (the game's log says
# which line and why), everything else still works. Keep it PG-13.
#
# ACT / ==== lines are just headings to find your way around; move characters about as you like.
